prompt: The line graph below shows the average daily water consumption per person in three cities between 1990 and 2015. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
modelAnswer:
The line graph compares the amount of water used each day by the average resident of three cities between 1990 and 2015.

Overall, water consumption fell steadily in City X, rose considerably in City Y and declined only slightly in City Z. As a result, the city with the lowest use in 1990 had the highest by the end of the period.

In 1990, City X residents used the most water, at 220 litres per person, compared with 160 litres in City Z and only 120 litres in City Y. Over the following 25 years, City X's figure dropped by 70 litres to 150 litres, with the fastest decrease occurring between 1995 and 2000.

By contrast, City Y's consumption rose in every period, climbing from 120 to 200 litres. It overtook City Z around 2005 and passed City X in 2010, when the two cities recorded 190 and 165 litres respectively.

City Z remained relatively stable, falling only from 160 to 145 litres, and by 2015 it had the lowest consumption of the three.
examinerComment: Clear overview, accurate data and good comparisons, including the points at which lines cross. Information is logically organised by city.
usefulPhrases: the fastest decrease occurred between ... and ...
